title: Introduce policy-translator and tenant-isolation overlay for installer automation
author: Asha Menon
description: Motivation: Private installer customers requested faster, auditable tenant bootstrap flows for RBAC and scoped service accounts; operators also wanted a single artifact that can compile policy bundles for both Helm and Terraform-driven installs. This PR introduces a small compiled utility (policy-translator), Helm tenant-overlay templates, and a Terraform rbac_bootstrap module. The translator consumes a canonical tenant policy YAML and emits both: (1) a namespaced Role/RoleBinding set suitable for post-install tenant reconciliation, and (2) a policy-bundle JSON that the private control plane can ingest for enrollment. Key user-visible outcomes: idempotent tenant bootstrap, deterministic policy bundle artifacts for audit, and a preflight check in the installer to surface missing permissions before applying resources. Summary of changes: - Add cmd/policy-translator: compiler that validates canonical tenant policies, computes least-privilege Role/RoleBinding, and outputs both Helm values overlays and terraform-compatible HCL snippets. The binary is gogo-based, with unit tests and a small OpenAPI-ish schema for the canonical format. - Helm: charts/tenant-overlay/ contains namespaced templates (Role, RoleBinding, ServiceAccount annotations) and a values schema to enable selective feature gates (kv-cache, metrics). - Terraform: modules/rbac_bootstrap/ implements idempotent apply using stateful locking and exposes a `policy_bundle` input to seed the installer-managed vault entries. - Installer: preflight step that runs policy-translator in dry-run mode, validates generated artifacts, and fails fast on disallowed cluster roles or missing KMS keys. - Tests: e2e/integration/tenant_rbac_test.go adds an end-to-end which spins up kind clusters and exercises translation -> helm template -> terraform plan -> apply dry-run. Backwards compatibility: existing private installs are untouched unless operator opts into the new `tenant_overlay` flow. Rollout plan: feature gated behind install flag `--enable-tenant-compiler`; rollout to staging for a week, then opt-in opens to GA. Security notes: translator validates service account scopes and denies translations that would map to builtin cluster-admin; audit logs are emitted to installer logs. Implementation details: the translator implements a small policy language with verbs/resource principals; it maps high-level capabilities (e.g., `manage.kv-prefix`) to concrete Role rules using a compiled rule table (extensible). The Helm overlay uses namePrefix/namespace templating to ensure tenant isolation. Terraform module uses remote state locking (dynamically chosen backend) to avoid races on concurrent tenant bootstraps. Upgrade/rollback: translator output is annotated with a `redwood.io/translator-version` label; the installer records last-applied bundle in the tenant namespace as a ConfigMap to allow safe rollbacks. Why unique: combines a cross-toolchain compiled artifact plus both Helm and Terraform plumbing and an installer preflight step; different from typical single-repo RBAC changes because it produces consumable policy bundles and enforces idempotent bootstrapping across tools.
